passages.text: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus went to eat a meal on the Sabbath.
He went to the house of a leading Pharisee.
Other people were there.
They watched Jesus closely.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκόν τινος τῶν ἀρχόντων τῶν Φαρισαίων σαββάτῳ φαγεῖν ἄρτον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦσαν παρατηρούμενοι αὐτόν

passages.text: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present in the house of a leading Pharisee on the Sabbath.
People were watching Jesus closely.
A man stood in front of Jesus.
This man had dropsy.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν ὑδρωπικὸς ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present in the home of a leading Pharisee on the Sabbath.
The Pharisees and experts in the law were there.
Jesus spoke to them.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς νομικοὺς καὶ Φαρισαίους λέγων Ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεῦσαι ἢ οὔ

passages.text: But they remained silent. Then Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
passages.sermon:
The experts in the law and the Pharisees did not answer Jesus.
They stayed silent.
Jesus took hold of the man with dropsy.
Jesus healed the man.
Jesus sent the man away.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἡσύχασαν Καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος ἰάσατο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπέλυσεν

passages.text: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the experts in the law and the Pharisees.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Suppose your son falls into a pit on the Sabbath day.
Or suppose your ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day.
Will you not immediately pull him out?”
passages.original: καὶ πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν Τίνος ὑμῶν υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς εἰς φρέαρ πεσεῖται καὶ οὐκ εὐθέως ἀνασπάσει αὐτὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου

passages.text: And they were unable to answer these questions.
passages.sermon:
The people listened to Jesus.
They heard His questions.
They could not answer Him.
They remained silent.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἀνταποκριθῆναι πρὸς ταῦτα

passages.text: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the guests choose the best seats.
Jesus spoke to the guests.
Jesus told them a parable.
Jesus said, “When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not sit in the place of honor.
Someone more important than you may also be invited.
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς κεκλημένους παραβολήν ἐπέχων πῶς τὰς πρωτοκλισίας ἐξελέγοντο λέγων πρὸς αὐτούς Ὅταν κληθῇς ὑπό τινος εἰς γάμους μὴ κατακλιθῇς εἰς τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν μή‿ ποτε ἐντιμότερός σου ᾖ κεκλημένος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the guests at the banquet.
He told them a parable about choosing seats of honor.
He said, the host invited both you and another guest.
The host will come to you.
He will say, “Give this man your seat.”
You will feel ashamed.
You will have to move to the last place.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ σὲ καὶ αὐτὸν καλέσας ἐρεῖ σοι Δὸς τούτῳ τόπον καὶ τότε ἄρξῃ μετὰ αἰσχύνης τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον κατέχειν

passages.text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the guests at a meal.
He noticed how they chose the best seats.
He told them a parable.
He said, "When someone invites you to a banquet, do not choose the place of honor.
Instead, go and sit in the lowest place.
Then your host will come to you.
He will say, 'Friend, move up to a better place.'
You will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you."
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ ὅταν κληθῇς πορευθεὶς ἀνάπεσε εἰς τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ κεκληκώς σε ἐρεῖ σοι Φίλε προσανάβηθι ἀνώτερον τότε ἔσται σοι δόξα ἐνώπιον πάντων τῶν συνανακειμένων σοι

passages.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He taught about pride and humility.
Every person who lifts himself up will be brought low.
Every person who makes himself low will be lifted up.
passages.original: ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται καὶ ὁ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται

passages.text: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man who had invited Him.
He said, "When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends.
Do not invite your brothers.
Do not invite your relatives.
Do not invite your rich neighbors.
If you invite them, they may invite you in return.
Then you will be repaid."
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους μή‿ ποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε καὶ γένηται ἀνταπόδομά σοι

passages.text: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind, and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man who had invited Him.
Jesus gave instructions about hosting a banquet.
He said, "When you host a banquet, invite the poor.
Invite the crippled.
Invite the lame.
Invite the blind.
You will be blessed.
They cannot repay you.
God will repay you at the resurrection of the righteous."
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ὅταν δοχὴν ποιῇς κάλει πτωχούς ἀναπείρους χωλούς τυφλούς καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων

passages.text: When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was eating with several people.
One of the people was sitting at the table with Jesus.
This man heard what Jesus said about inviting the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind to a banquet.
The man spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δέ τις τῶν συνανακειμένων ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῷ Μακάριος ὅστις φάγεται ἄρτον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus told a story.
A certain man planned a great banquet.
This man prepared a large meal.
He invited many guests to his banquet.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἄνθρωπός τις ἐποίει δεῖπνον μέγα καὶ ἐκάλεσεν πολλούς

passages.text: When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
passages.sermon:
A certain man prepared a great banquet.
He invited many guests.
The time for the banquet arrived.
The man sent his servant.
He told his servant to speak to the invited guests.
He told the servant to say, “Come.”
He said, “Everything is now ready.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ δείπνου εἰπεῖν τοῖς κεκλημένοις Ἔρχεσθε ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ἐστιν

passages.text: But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a story about a man who invited many guests to a great banquet.
The invited guests began to make excuses, one after another.
The first guest spoke to the servant.
He said, "I have bought a field."
He said, "I need to go and see it."
He said, "Please excuse me."
passages.original: Καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀπὸ μιᾶς πάντες παραιτεῖσθαι ὁ πρῶτος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀγρὸν ἠγόρασα καὶ ἔχω ἀνάγκην ἐξελθὼν ἰδεῖν αὐτόν ἐρωτῶ σε ἔχε με παρῃτημένον

passages.text: Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’
passages.sermon:
A second man spoke.
He said, “I have bought five pairs of oxen.”
He said, “I am going to test them.”
He said, “Please excuse me.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν Ζεύγη βοῶν ἠγόρασα πέντε καὶ πορεύομαι δοκιμάσαι αὐτά ἐρωτῶ σε ἔχε με παρῃτημένον

passages.text: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’
passages.sermon: A man spoke to the servant.\r\nHe said, “I have married a wife.”\r\nHe said, “Because of this, I cannot come.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν Γυναῖκα ἔγημα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐ δύναμαι ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: The servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’
passages.sermon:
A servant returned to his master.
The servant reported everything to his master.
The master owned the house.
The master became angry.
The master spoke to his servant.
The master said, "Go out quickly."
He told the servant to go into the streets and alleys of the city.
He told the servant to bring in the poor.
He told the servant to bring in the crippled.
He told the servant to bring in the blind.
He told the servant to bring in the lame.
passages.original: Καὶ παραγενόμενος ὁ δοῦλος ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα τότε ὀργισθεὶς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἶπεν τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ Ἔξελθε ταχέως εἰς τὰς πλατείας καὶ ῥύμας τῆς πόλεως καὶ τοὺς πτωχοὺς καὶ ἀναπείρους καὶ τυφλοὺς καὶ χωλοὺς εἰσάγαγε ὧδε

passages.text: ‘Sir,’ the servant replied, ‘what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’
passages.sermon: A servant spoke to his master.\r\nThe servant said, “Sir, I have done what you commanded.”\r\nThe servant said, “There is still room.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ δοῦλος Κύριε γέγονεν ὃ ἐπέταξας καὶ ἔτι τόπος ἐστίν

passages.text: So the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to his servant.
The master gave a command.
He said, "Go out to the roads and the fences."
He told the servant to find people there.
He said, "Compel them to come in."
The master wanted his house to be full.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν δοῦλον Ἔξελθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς καὶ ἀνάγκασον εἰσελθεῖν ἵνα γεμισθῇ μου ὁ οἶκος

passages.text: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said this about those who were invited to the banquet.
None of those men who were invited will eat at my banquet.
Not one of them will taste my feast.
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κεκλημένων γεύσεταί μου τοῦ δείπνου

passages.text: Large crowds were now traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them, “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters—yes, even his own life—he cannot be My disciple.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled with many people.
Large crowds followed Him.
Jesus turned to the crowds.
He spoke to them.
Jesus said, “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father, he cannot be My disciple.
If anyone does not hate his mother, he cannot be My disciple.
If anyone does not hate his wife, he cannot be My disciple.
If anyone does not hate his children, he cannot be My disciple.
If anyone does not hate his brothers, he cannot be My disciple.
If anyone does not hate his sisters, he cannot be My disciple.
If anyone does not hate even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.”
passages.original: Συνεπορεύοντο δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί καὶ στραφεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Εἴ τις ἔρχεται πρός με καὶ οὐ μισεῖ τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τὰς ἀδελφάς ἔτι τε καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἑαυτοῦ οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής

passages.text: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the large crowds traveling with Him.
He said these words to them.
A person must carry his own cross.
A person must follow Jesus.
If a person does not carry his cross and follow Jesus, he cannot be a disciple of Jesus.
passages.original: ὅστις οὐ βαστάζει τὸν σταυρὸν ἑαυτοῦ καὶ ἔρχεται ὀπίσω μου οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής

passages.text: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to a large crowd.
He gave them an example.
He said, “Suppose one of you wants to build a tower.
You must first sit down.
You must count the cost.
You must see if you have enough resources to finish it.”
passages.original: Τίς γὰρ ἐξ ὑμῶν θέλων πύργον οἰκοδομῆσαι οὐχὶ πρῶτον καθίσας ψηφίζει τὴν δαπάνην εἰ ἔχει εἰς ἀπαρτισμόν

passages.text: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him, saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’
passages.sermon:
A man wants to build a tower.
He lays the foundation.
He cannot finish the work.
People see this.
They begin to mock him.
They say, “This man started to build.
He could not finish.”
passages.original: ἵνα μή ποτε θέντος αὐτοῦ θεμέλιον καὶ μὴ ἰσχύοντος ἐκτελέσαι πάντες οἱ θεωροῦντες ἄρξωνται αὐτῷ ἐμπαίζειν λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἤρξατο οἰκοδομεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἐκτελέσαι

passages.text: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
passages.sermon:
A king leads his army to fight another king.
He prepares to go to war.
He knows the other king is coming against him.
The other king has twenty thousand men.
This king has ten thousand men.
Before the battle, the king sits down.
He thinks carefully.
He asks himself if he can fight with only ten thousand men.
He considers if he is able to face the king with twenty thousand men.
passages.original: Ἢ τίς βασιλεὺς πορευόμενος ἑτέρῳ βασιλεῖ συμβαλεῖν εἰς πόλεμον οὐχὶ καθίσας πρῶτον βουλεύσεται εἰ δυνατός ἐστιν ἐν δέκα χιλιάσιν ὑπαντῆσαι τῷ μετὰ εἴκοσι χιλιάδων ἐρχομένῳ ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.
passages.sermon:
A king prepares to go to war against another king.
He first considers if he can win with his ten thousand soldiers against the other king’s twenty thousand soldiers.
If the king decides he cannot win,
and while the other king is still far away,
he sends a group of messengers.
He asks the other king for peace.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ἔτι αὐτοῦ πόρρω ὄντος πρεσβείαν ἀποστείλας ἐρωτᾷ τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην

passages.text: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to a crowd.
He taught about following Him.
He said, “Anyone who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.”
He meant that you must let go of all you own to follow Him.
You cannot be His disciple unless you do this.
passages.original: Οὕτως οὖν πᾶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ὃς οὐκ ἀποτάσσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὑπάρχουσιν οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής

passages.text: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?
passages.sermon:
Salt is good.
Salt has value.
Salt must keep its flavor.
If salt loses its flavor, it cannot season anything.
Nothing can make flavorless salt useful again.
passages.original: Καλὸν οὖν τὸ ἅλας ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ ἐν τίνι ἀρτυθήσεται

passages.text: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said some things are not useful.
This salt is not good for the soil.
This salt is not good for the manure pile.
People throw it away.
If you have ears, listen to this.
passages.original: οὔτε εἰς γῆν οὔτε εἰς κοπρίαν εὔθετόν ἐστιν ἔξω βάλλουσιν αὐτό Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω
